speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with chronic left shoulder pain without a history of trauma. To begin our evaluation, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what activities make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old woman. The patient reports a 2-month history of insidious onset left shoulder pain, worsening with extreme ranges of motion and activity. Pain disrupts sleep, and there's noted difficulty with activities of daily living like brushing hair and dressing. No history of shoulder trauma, neck pain, arm/hand weakness, numbness, or paresthesias. The patient has type 2 diabetes mellitus, treated with metformin and glipizide.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details, Mrs. Jones. Given your age, the insidious onset of pain, difficulty with overhead activities (brushing hair), and your history of Type 2 diabetes, I am concerned about a rotator cuff tear or tendinopathy. Can you tell me specifically if you feel any weakness when trying to lift your arm up, or if it hurts more when you reach behind your back?
